newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai rice mixed, better performance seen in H2.
newsitem.headline: Thai rice mixed, better performance seen in H2.

text.p: Thai rice prices were steady to higher this week as exporters sought fragrant rice to meet obligations, traders said on Thursday.
The market was quiet with only small orders in place. There was market talk that Iran might enter the market again but traders said Tehran was likely to opt for Vietnam rice this time.
Major activities in the market were contracts covering mostly to the Philippines, which earlier this year bought a substantial amount of lower-grade rice, and to Hong Kong.
"The prices of lower grade rice was not affected despite the demand as most exporters who sold to the Philippines had covered already their positions," said one trader.
"But fragrant rice edged up due to liftings to Hong Kong and Malaysia and also to tight supplies," he said.

Thai benchmark 100 percent B grade rice was unchanged at $320-360 per tonne FOB Bangkok while the price of 100 percent fragrant rice rose to $700-720 per tonne on the same basis against $690-710 last week.
The market continued to watch development of the El Nino effect in other rice producing and buying countries.
However, market sources said they did not think that a lower-than expected amount of rains, and dryness in some areas in Thailand was related to El Nino.
"The rain is a bit late this year. But this is not unusual. I will start to worry if there is no rain in July," said one exporter.
"In Thailand, farmers normally start planting after the Buddhist Lent which takes place next month," he said.
A senior commerce ministry official said he expected Thai rice sales to improve during the second half of 1997, especially if El Nino took its toll in the region.
He said there would be more rice auctions in Japan, South Korea and by World Food Program during that period.
"Thailand were barely affected in the past. And we hope not this year," said the official.
"We should be able to see more clearly which country will be affected by drought brought about by the El Nino effect by August," he said.
Thailand has so far exported around 2.1 million tonnes of rice this year.
